correctness.rationale: The proof first shows that a connected dominating set must contain at least two vertices from each bipartition side. Those inequalities are also sufficient for domination. The induced selected graph is a complete bipartite graph with only matched diagonal edges removed; a component-separation argument shows that it is disconnected exactly when each side has two selected vertices with the same two indices. Exact counting yields the polynomial. A deletion argument then proves that every inclusion-minimal connected dominating set has size 4. The standalone exhaustive checker independently verifies every subset for n=3 through 9, all 91 polynomial coefficients, the minimum multiplicity, total count, and inclusion-minimal classification.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a standard symmetric family, and connected domination is a classical structural parameter with direct links to maximum-leaf spanning trees and, more recently, binomial-edge-ideal v-numbers. The same-object literature had only the scalar minimum value. The all-set theorem is a natural complete classification that simultaneously gives the exact family polynomial, every minimum set, the total count, and the fact that no larger inclusion-minimal connected dominating sets exist. This is structurally stronger than a routine recomputation of gamma_c=4.
